c.tagline: Mediterranean port city cascading down Mount Carmel to the golden-domed Bahá'í Gardens.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis (monit) are legally required to run the meter (moneh); insist on it, especially from the airport or train station, since some drivers may push for a flat rate instead.

emergency.note: 102 reaches fire and rescue services; 100 and 101 are the most commonly used emergency numbers in daily life.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Safe; follow local security guidance given regional tensions

hood_desc: A restored 19th-century Templer colony of stone houses turned into cafes, restaurants and galleries, running straight up to the foot of the Bahá'í Gardens; best for first-time visitors who want the signature view and easy dining.
A historic Arab-Christian neighborhood known for its market, murals and mixed Jewish-Arab street life; suits travelers wanting an authentic, less touristy feel and some of the city's best hummus.
A dense commercial district partway up the mountain with the Carmelit funicular's lower stations, markets and budget shopping; central and convenient though less polished than the areas above it.
The upscale plateau atop Mount Carmel with panoramic promenades, business hotels and the university nearby; suits travelers wanting views, quieter streets and higher-end lodging.
A seafront strip near the beach, the cable car up to Stella Maris and Rambam hospital; good for travelers wanting beach access and a quieter, more local feel.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: Buses and the Carmelit generally run from around 5:30 AM to midnight on weekdays; nearly all public transport, including the Carmelit, shuts down from Friday afternoon until Saturday evening for Shabbat.
transit.pay: Pay with a rechargeable Rav-Kav smart card (available at kiosks and stations) or through the Moovit app; cash fares are also accepted on board buses.
transit.note: Haifa is the only Israeli city with an underground rail system, the six-station Carmelit funicular linking downtown to Mount Carmel; it's the oldest underground transit system in the Middle East.

air: Ben Gurion Airport (TLV), near Tel Aviv
Haifa Airport (HFA) - limited regional flights to Athens and Larnaca
train: Israel Railways coastal line (Haifa–Tel Aviv–Ben Gurion Airport)
Israel Railways Jezreel Valley line (Haifa–Beit She'an via Afula)
bus: Egged and Nateev Express city/regional buses

transit.m: Israel Railways direct train, Ben Gurion Airport–Haifa (~55-70 min)
Nateev Express intercity bus or shared taxi (sherut)

tip.r: Around 12% is standard at restaurants and is sometimes added automatically for larger groups; tipping taxi drivers isn't required but rounding up is common.
